name: Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park
note: National park (large, north of Sydney on Broken Bay and the Hawkesbury): bushwalks, Aboriginal rock art, boat access; Wikivoyage and NPWS name it.

name: Bobbin Head
note: Picnic and boat-hire area on the Cowan Creek side of Ku-ring-gai Chase with the Kalkari/Bobbin Head information centre; a Wikivoyage section.

name: Kalkari Discovery Centre
note: Visitor and discovery centre in Ku-ring-gai Chase with Aboriginal rock art and history displays (visitor centre; judge whether it is a standalone stop).

name: West Head
note: Headland lookout and walking area at the western end of Ku-ring-gai Chase with Aboriginal art sites and the Aboriginal Heritage Walk.

name: Aboriginal Heritage Walk (West Head)
note: Walking track (4.4 km loop) through Aboriginal rock art and engravings at West Head; part of the West Head area, listed separately by Wikivoyage.

name: Barrenjoey Lighthouse
note: Heritage sandstone lighthouse (1881) at the tip of Palm Beach; a walk up to the headland with views across Broken Bay; guided tours on set days.

name: Palm Beach
note: Beach and village at the northern tip of the Northern Beaches on Pittwater; named by Wikivoyage as the northern end of the beaches, with Barrenjoey and the Home and Away filming sites.

name: Whale Beach
note: Calm surf beach with a rose-gold sand cove between cliffs; Wikivoyage names it as a peaceful beach.

name: Mona Vale Beach
note: Long golden surf beach with parking and lifeguard patrols; Wikivoyage lists it among the Northern Beaches beaches.

name: Warriewood Beach
note: Small sheltered beach with headlands and a trail down from the top; Wikivoyage calls it one of the most picturesque on the peninsula.

name: Curl Curl Rock Pool
note: Ocean rock pool (about 50 m) at South Curl Curl; Wikivoyage names it as a swimming spot.
coordinates_source: openstreetmap leisure=swimming_pool (South Curl Curl Rock Pool)

name: Pittwater
note: Waterway (inlet of Broken Bay) along the northern peninsula; Wikivoyage names its attractive beaches and scenery. Long water feature; visitors reach it from Palm Beach, Church Point and Mona Vale.

name: Dee Why Lagoon
note: Nature reserve and wetland behind Dee Why Beach, bird-watching (best viewed from Long Reef); Wikivoyage names it.

name: Dural Lane Murals
note: Street murals in Hornsby depicting the early 20th-century town; a free walk-up art attraction named on Wikivoyage.

name: Ku-ring-gai Wildflower Garden
note: Native plant garden in St Ives with bushland walks; open daily; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Rose Seidler House
note: Harry Seidler's 1950 modernist house in Wahroonga, open to visitors as a museum (Sydney Living Museums); Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Seven Little Australians Park
note: Bushland park with a hiking trail in Gordon, named for the children's novel; Wikivoyage lists it as a recreation site.

name: Lindfield Rocks
note: Sandstone bouldering and climbing site in East Lindfield, the oldest bouldering site in Sydney; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Muru Mittigar
note: Aboriginal cultural education centre at Rouse Hill with bush tucker tours and talks; bookings essential (Wikivoyage Hills; sydney.com Blacktown).

name: Museums Discovery Centre
note: Historical-objects museum at Castle Hill; Wikivoyage notes it was closed temporarily (status unverified).

name: Rouse Hill House and Farm
note: Colonial homestead and farm museum in Rouse Hill run by Sydney Living Museums; not named by the counted sources checked so far.

name: Cattai National Park
note: National park on the Hawkesbury River with Cattai Farm (1821 First Fleet surgeon's farm and windmill ruins); camping, canoeing, picnics. Wikivoyage Hills and NPWS name it.

name: Marramarra National Park
note: National park at the junction of the Hawkesbury River and Berowra Creek: canoeing, kayaking, bushwalking and camping; NPWS and Wikivoyage name it.

name: Scheyville National Park
note: National park near Windsor with the Scheyville migrant camp heritage walk, Longneck Lagoon and horse-riding trails; NPWS and Wikivoyage name it.

name: Dharug National Park
note: National park on the Hawkesbury north of Wisemans Ferry; Old Great North Road World Heritage walk, canoeing and mountain biking; NPWS and Wikivoyage name it.

name: Muogamarra Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve on the Hawkesbury with Aboriginal engravings and wildflowers; open to the public only about six weeks a year on booked volunteer-guided tours (NPWS).

name: Old Great North Road
note: World Heritage convict-built road between Wisemans Ferry and Wiseman's area, walkable; Wikivoyage calls it the Great North Road Convict Trail, NPWS calls it the Old Great North Road walk.

name: Wisemans Ferry
note: Village and river crossing on the Hawkesbury, gateway to Dharug and Yengo parks; ferry crossing itself is the way across, not a separate spot. Wikivoyage names the town park and village.

name: Tobruk Sheep Station
note: Working sheep station at Maroota with sheep-dog and shearing shows, $5 entry; permanent farm attraction named by Wikivoyage.

name: Brooklyn
note: Fishing and boating town on the Hawkesbury River, gateway to Ku-ring-gai Chase and the Great North Walk; ferry to Dangar Island. Wikivoyage names it.

name: Hawkesbury River
note: Long river (the Hawkesbury) through the north-west fringe, with boating, houseboats, canoeing and the Ku-ring-gai Chase shoreline; long feature visited from its towns.

name: Windsor
note: Historic colonial town on the Hawkesbury with Georgian buildings and the Macquarie Arms on the river; the City of Hawkesbury hub named by Wikivoyage.

name: Richmond
note: Historic farming town (settled 1794) on the Hawkesbury, home to the RAAF base; Wikivoyage covers it in the City of Hawkesbury article.

name: RAAF Museum
note: Aviation museum at RAAF Base Richmond with historic aircraft; free to visit (confirm access). Not named by the counted sources checked (Wikivoyage Richmond/Hawkesbury page does not mention it).

name: Hawkesbury Regional Museum
note: Small regional museum in Windsor on the history of the Hawkesbury; free entry, open most days except Tuesdays.

name: Tebbutt's Observatory
note: Historic observatory and Peninsula House in Windsor, a Hawkesbury Museum heritage site about 15 minutes' walk from the town centre.

name: Australiana Pioneer Village
note: Volunteer-run pioneer village at Wilberforce with historic buildings and equipment rides, open Sundays and Bank Holiday Mondays only.

name: Trees Adventure Grose River Park
note: Operator: treetop aerial adventure course at Yarramundi, Grose River Park (Trees Adventure company); a private operator, judge as an operator.

name: Penrith
note: Regional city at the western end of the Sydney basin, base for the Blue Mountains, Nepean River and western attractions; Wikivoyage Outer West names it as the main centre.

name: Nepean River
note: River running through Penrith and Camden with riverside parks and walking paths; Wikivoyage names its parks alongside the river.

name: Penrith Whitewater Stadium
note: Man-made whitewater course built for the 2000 Olympics at Cranebrook; rafting and kayaking open to the public; Wikivoyage and sydney.com name it.

name: Sydney International Regatta Centre
note: Rowing and paddling lake (Penrith Lakes, Castlereagh) built for the 2000 Olympics; open daily outside event days (Wikivoyage Outer West).

name: Western Sydney Parklands
note: Large public parkland across western Sydney with cycling, Treetops, Sydney Zoo and Chang Lai Yuan gardens; a park system rather than one stop.

name: Sydney Zoo
note: Zoo in the Western Sydney Parklands at Bungarribee/Eastern Creek with walk-through safari-style exhibits and elephants; sydney.com names it.

name: WILD LIFE Sydney Zoo
note: Zoo at Darling Harbour in the Sydney CBD, zoned by Australian habitat; sydney.com names it. Inside the existing Sydney destination span, not yet in the app. Separate venue from the existing Sea Life Sydney Aquarium spot, though they share the Darling Harbour / King Street Wharf area.

name: Sydney Motorsport Park
note: Motor-racing circuit complex at Eastern Creek with public experiences (The Apex V8 ride, karting, Sydney Dragway); permanent venue, judge the public-experience side.

name: Sydney Action Park
note: Water park at Prospect (opened 2013 as Wet'n'Wild Sydney, renamed Raging Waters Sydney 2019); seasonal opening. A DNSW search result names Raging Waters, but the page was not fetched, so no counted source yet.

name: TreeTops Adventure Park
note: Rope and tree-course adventure park in the Western Sydney Parklands with more than 90 aerial obstacles; sydney.com names it (operator).

name: iFLY Penrith
note: Operator: indoor skydiving wind tunnel in Penrith; sydney.com names it.

name: Cables Wake Park
note: Operator: cable-skiing and wakeboard lake in Penrith; sydney.com names it.

name: Blacktown Sportspark
note: Sports complex (former Olympic venue) in Blacktown; sport fields, not a visitor draw by itself; listed for the judge.

name: Parramatta
note: Second CBD and historic city, 24 km west of Sydney; Wikivoyage describes its parks, colonial buildings and ferry trip up the river.

name: Parramatta Park
note: Large parkland with the Old Government House, tudor gatehouses, Governor's Bath House and cycling tracks; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Experiment Farm Cottage
note: Colonial cottage at Harris Park, the first private farm in Australia, run by the National Trust; open Wednesday to Sunday.

name: Hambledon Cottage
note: Colonial Georgian cottage built by John Macarthur in 1824 on the Harris Park heritage walk; open Thursday to Sunday.

name: Brislington House
note: Former residence (1821) turned museum of Parramatta medical and nursing history; limited opening hours.

name: Lancer Barracks
note: Historic army barracks beside Parramatta station with the Linden House Museum of the Royal NSW Lancers.

name: Female Factory Precinct
note: Convict women's establishment site (1821) at Parramatta, a UNESCO World Heritage convict site; Wikivoyage names the Female Factory.

name: Female Orphan School
note: Australia's first purpose-built charitable institution building (Western Sydney University campus, Parramatta); exterior visible from the campus.

name: St Patrick's Cathedral, Parramatta
note: Catholic cathedral in central Parramatta on Marsden Street; Wikivoyage lists it on the Parramatta walk.

name: Prince Alfred Park
note: Central Parramatta park on the site of the colony's first gaol, opposite St Patrick's Cathedral; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Lake Parramatta
note: Reserve and lake about 2 km north of the Parramatta CBD, walking and picnics; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Queens Wharf Reserve
note: Parramatta riverside reserve where Governor Phillip first landed, with ship memorials; on the Harris Park heritage walk.

name: Powerhouse Parramatta
note: Museum of applied arts and sciences being built on the Parramatta River; Wikivoyage says it is under construction (check opening status).

name: Camden
note: Historic country town on the Nepean with its Argyle Street cafes and museums; Wikivoyage Camden article.

name: Camden Museum
note: Historical museum in Camden run by the Camden Historical Society; free admission, Thursday to Sunday.

name: Camden Park Estate
note: Historic Macarthur family estate at Camden; not named by a counted source checked so far (judge access).

name: Campbelltown
note: Regional city at the centre of the Macarthur district, with the Campbelltown Arts Centre and heritage walks; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Campbelltown Arts Centre
note: Free regional art gallery with a Japanese garden and teahouse, a short walk from Campbelltown CBD; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Ultimate Paintball
note: Operator: 120-acre paintball park at Camden Park with themed battlefields; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: E. G. Waterhouse National Camellia Garden
wiki: E. G. Waterhouse National Camellia Garden
note: Public garden of camellias in Caringbah with playground and cafe; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Joseph Banks Native Plants Reserve
note: Native plant reserve at Kareela with a large collection of Australian plants; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Towra Point Nature Reserve
note: Wetland reserve on Botany Bay for migratory birds; mostly closed to visitors, with a visitor centre (Wikivoyage says mostly not open).

name: Captain Cook's Landing Place
note: Site at Kurnell where Cook first landed in 1770: the landing rock, monuments and a visitor centre; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Royal National Park
note: National park south of Sydney (1879, second-oldest in the world) with coastal walks, lagoons and heritage sites; NPWS, Wikivoyage and sydney.com name it.

name: Audley
note: Historic boat shed, cafe and picnic area on the Hacking River inside Royal National Park; the park's main visitor hub with canoe hire.

name: Bungoona Lookout
note: Paved lookout over the Hacking River valley in Royal National Park, suitable for strollers; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Wedding Cake Rock
note: Sandstone rock formation on the Coast Track in Royal National Park that looks like a wedding cake; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Figure Eight Pools
note: Figure-eight shaped rock pools below Burning Palms; reached by a scramble, only safe at low tide and sometimes underwater; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Uloola Falls
note: Waterfall in Royal National Park reached by a fire-road walk from Waterfall station; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Wattamolla Beach
note: Lagoon and beach in Royal National Park reached by car via Audley; swimming and picnics; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Garie Beach
note: Surf beach in Royal National Park reached by road, patrolled on summer weekends; whale and bird watching; Wikivoyage names it.

name: North Era Beach
note: Beach in Royal National Park with a camping permit area; reached by a 30-45 minute walk; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Burning Palms Beach
note: Remote beach in Royal National Park reached by a steep walk down from Garrawarra Farm or along the Coast Track; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Werrong Beach
note: Clothing-optional beach in Royal National Park reached by a steep walk from Otford; Wikivoyage names it.

name: Big Marley Beach
note: Unpatrolled beach in Royal National Park reached only on foot; Wikivoyage names Big and Little Marley.

name: Bundeena
note: Village on the Port Hacking reached by ferry from Cronulla; northern gateway to the Royal National Park Coast Track; sydney.com names it.

name: Bundeena to Otford Coast Track
note: 30 km coastal walk through Royal National Park from Bundeena to Otford, passing most of the park's beaches; a multi-day or day-section walk.

name: Nattai National Park
note: Remote sandstone park in the Wollondilly hinterland near Oakdale and Mittagong, bushwalks and backpack camping; NPWS names it (Wikivoyage Macarthur names the wider area).

name: Thirlmere Lakes National Park
note: World Heritage lakes (part of the Greater Blue Mountains Area) near Picton with walking tracks; Wikivoyage and NPWS name it.

name: Picton
note: Historic village on the Southern Highlands line with Argyle Street pubs, the Victoria Bridge and walks; Wikivoyage names it as the Wollondilly town.

name: Mushroom Tunnel
note: Old railway tunnel relic on Argyle Street in Picton; a short walk through; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Victoria Bridge, Picton
note: Historic trestle bridge over Stonequarry Creek in Picton; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Burragorang Lookout
note: Lookout over Lake Burragorang and the Burragorang Valley; Wikivoyage names it as a Picton attraction.

name: Lake Burragorang
note: Reservoir behind Warragamba Dam, a large lake with lookouts and boating in the Burragorang Valley; Wikivoyage names the valley and lookout.

name: Warragamba Dam
note: Large dam wall on the Warragamba River, Sydney's main water supply; viewing from the road (judge public access).

name: The Oaks
note: Village in the Wollondilly shire near Thirlmere and the Burragorang; Wikivoyage names it as a place to explore.

name: Yerranderie
note: Former silver-mining town in the Wollondilly hinterland with a restored heritage site, reached by a long unsealed road; not named by a counted source checked yet.

name: Sydney Skydivers
note: Operator: skydiving from Wilton airfield near Picton; Wikivoyage names it (operator, judge with the other operators).
